c10_bio_ch01.task: Chew a small piece of plain roti or bread for a full minute without swallowing — notice it turns sweet. Note which enzyme acted and where digestion began.

c10_bio_ch02.task: In a dim room, watch your pupil in a mirror while a family member brings a phone torch near (not directly into) your face. Record how the pupil responds to light.

c10_bio_ch03.task: Find a potato with 'eyes', a ginger rhizome or an onion base at home. Plant or soak it and note which part sprouts — vegetative propagation in action.

c10_bio_ch04.task: Survey 5 inherited traits (free/attached earlobes, tongue rolling, dimples, widow's peak, bent thumb) across your family; tally counts in a table and guess the dominant form.

c10_chem_ch01.task: Add a pinch of baking soda to a spoon of vinegar or lemon juice in a cup. Note the gas evolved and any temperature change, then write the word equation.

c10_chem_ch02.task: Make a natural indicator: steep grated beetroot (or hibiscus/tea) in warm water. Test drops on soap solution, lemon juice and baking-soda solution; tabulate the colours.

c10_chem_ch03.task: Place an iron nail in water, one coated with oil, and one in a dry spot. Check daily for 3 days and record which rusts — the conditions corrosion needs.

c10_chem_ch04.task: Hold a steel spoon high above a candle flame (with an adult) for a few seconds, then wipe the black deposit. Identify it as soot and link it to incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon.

c10_chem_ch05.task: Hunt the periodic table at home: find iron (nail), aluminium (foil), copper (wire/coin), carbon (pencil lead), calcium (chalk/eggshell), gold or silver (jewellery). List each with symbol, atomic number and metal/non-metal.

c10_math_ch01.task: Use prime factorisation to find the HCF and LCM of two real counts at home (e.g., 48 biscuits and 36 toffees); use the HCF to split them into identical packs.

c10_math_ch02.task: Build the product (x+a)(x+b) with paper strips: draw a rectangle of sides (x+a) and (x+b), split it into four regions and verify x²+(a+b)x+ab by measuring areas.

c10_math_ch03.task: Turn a grocery bill into equations: pick two items and write a pair like 3x+2y=total using two different shopping days' totals, then solve for each item's price.

c10_math_ch04.task: Arrange 24 coins or bottle caps in a rectangle whose length is 2 more than its breadth. Solve l(l−2)=24 and check it against your rectangle.

c10_math_ch05.task: Stack books or steel glasses in rows of 4, 7, 10, ... — predict the 8th row and the total items used with AP formulas, then verify by counting.

c10_math_ch06.task: Measure the shadow of a bottle and of a wall or gate at the same moment; use similar triangles to calculate the wall's height, then sanity-check it.

c10_math_ch07.task: Make a coordinate map of one room: treat each floor tile (or taped grid squares) as 1 unit, assign coordinates to 5 objects, and compute distances between them.

c10_math_ch08.task: Draw a right triangle on paper, measure its sides, compute sin, cos and tan of one acute angle, and verify sin²θ+cos²θ=1 from your own numbers.

c10_math_ch09.task: From your window, estimate the angle of elevation to the top of a nearby building or tree (paper clinometer: protractor + thread + straw) and its distance — compute its height.

c10_math_ch10.task: Trace a plate, draw a radius to the rim and a tangent at that point; verify with a protractor that radius ⟂ tangent. Then draw two tangents from an outside point and compare their lengths.

c10_math_ch11.task: Wrap a thread around a glass or bangle to measure its circumference; find the radius and compute the area it covers — compare with πr².

c10_math_ch12.task: Measure a bottle's height and diameter, compute its volume in cm³, and compare with the mL printed on its label. How close is the bottle to a true cylinder?

c10_math_ch13.task: Record the ages or heights of everyone at home; compute the mean, median and mode and decide which best represents your family.

c10_math_ch14.task: Toss a coin 50 times and tally heads; compare your experimental probability with ½, then repeat for a button or drawing-pin landing face-up.

c10_phy_ch01.task: Read the wattage labels on 5 devices (bulb, fan, charger, fridge, TV); rank them by power and estimate the units (kWh) one uses in a month.

c10_phy_ch02.task: Place a compass next to a charging cable while a phone charges, then when unplugged. Note any needle deflection — a current's magnetic field (observe only, no dismantling).

c10_phy_ch03.task: Fill two identical cups with equal water; put one in direct sun and one in shade for an hour. Compare temperatures and link the difference to solar energy.

c10_phy_ch04.task: Look at your reflection on the inner and outer sides of a steel spoon. Describe which side behaves concave or convex and how the image changes as you move it.

c11_bio_ch01.task: Catalogue 10 different living things visible from your home or window; classify each as plant, animal or microbe-sign and note one feature of each.

c11_bio_ch02.task: Build a dichotomous key for 8 household plants or food items (e.g., coriander vs mint, dal vs rice) using yes/no observable traits.

c11_bio_ch03.task: Look for a 'primitive' plant at home — moss on a damp wall, a fern, or green film in a water pot. Note its habitat and whether you can spot spores or seeds.

c11_bio_ch04.task: Observe an ant trail, spider, house gecko or cockroach from a safe distance. Note body symmetry, segments and leg count, and guess its phylum.

c11_bio_ch05.task: Uproot a small grass plant or examine a potted plant: sketch and label root, stem and leaf; note fibrous vs tap root and the leaf's venation pattern.

c11_bio_ch06.task: Compare the upper and lower surfaces of a leaf under a magnifier or phone macro lens; look for pores (stomata) and veins — anatomy visible from outside.

c11_bio_ch07.task: Find an earthworm after rain or watch a gecko closely: count body segments or rings and note symmetry and movement — structural organisation you can see.

c11_bio_ch08.task: Peel the thin inner skin of an onion scale, spread it on a clean glass with a drop of water, and view through a magnifier or phone macro — hunt for the 'brick-wall' cells.

c11_bio_ch09.task: Do the translucent-spot test: rub butter, oil, plain water and honey on separate paper squares, hold each to the light — which leave fat spots? Tabulate biomolecules in your kitchen.

c11_bio_ch10.task: Suspend an onion over water so its base just touches the surface; watch roots grow over 4-5 days and mark the fast-growing tips — where cells divide.

c11_bio_ch11.task: Cover part of a healthy potted leaf with foil for 3 days without detaching it; compare the covered and exposed regions — what did light do?

c11_bio_ch12.task: Seal a handful of sprouted moong beans in one jar and dry beans in another overnight; feel which jar is warmer — respiration releases heat.

c11_bio_ch13.task: Grow two bean seedlings — one on a bright sill, one in a dark cupboard. After 4 days compare height, colour and stem thickness — etiolation.

c11_bio_ch14.task: Wrap a measuring tape around your chest at the ribs; record normal exhale vs deepest inhale — measure the expansion your breathing muscles create.

c11_bio_ch15.task: Find your pulse at the wrist; count beats for 15 s ×4 while sitting, then again after 20 stair-climbs. Record both and explain the difference.

c11_bio_ch16.task: Track your water intake and note urine colour across one day (pale vs dark); relate the colour to how hard your kidneys are concentrating it.

c11_bio_ch17.task: Hold a water bottle, bend and straighten your elbow slowly; feel the front and back of your upper arm — identify the antagonistic muscle pair.

c11_bio_ch18.task: Two-point test: a partner touches your forearm with one or two pencil tips while you look away — find the smallest gap you can still tell is two points.

c11_bio_ch19.task: Measure your pulse and breathing at rest, then right after a startling moment (a jump-scare clip works); record the surge — adrenaline's chemical coordination.

c11_chem_ch01.task: Measure out one 'mole' at home: ~18 mL of water and ~58 g of table salt on a kitchen scale. Each holds ≈6×10²³ particles — feel Avogadro's number.

c11_chem_ch02.task: With an adult, sprinkle a pinch of salt near the edge of a gas flame and note the yellow tinge — sodium's electron transitions colour the flame.

c11_chem_ch03.task: Collect a steel spoon, aluminium foil, a copper item, a plastic spoon and chalk; tabulate lustre, hardness, heat conduction and magnetism — periodic trends in a drawer.

c11_chem_ch04.task: With an adult, heat a pinch of sugar and of salt separately in old spoons over low heat: sugar melts and chars, salt doesn't — covalent vs ionic bonding.

c11_chem_ch05.task: Seal air in a syringe or squeeze bottle and press — it compresses; try the same filled with water. Record which state of matter yields.

c11_chem_ch06.task: Dissolve a spoon each of salt, sugar and baking soda in three identical cups of water; feel each cup's outside — which dissolved endothermically or exothermically?

c11_chem_ch07.task: Leave a sealed half-full bottle in the sun; watch droplets form on the inner top — evaporation and condensation reaching equilibrium in a closed system.

c11_chem_ch08.task: Cut an apple; rub lemon juice on one half only. Compare browning after 30 minutes — oxidation vs the antioxidant effect.

c11_chem_ch09.task: Compare soap lather in tap water vs boiled/RO water (or rainwater); note which foams more — hard water and dissolved minerals.

c11_math_ch01.task: Sort a kitchen drawer or your bookshelf into sets (spoons/forks/knives or fiction/non-fiction); list the elements, then find the union, intersection and a proper subset.

c11_math_ch02.task: Write the relation 'is older than' as ordered pairs for your family; decide whether it is a function — and whether 'birth month of' is one-one or many-one.

c11_math_ch03.task: Mark 0°,30°,45°,60°,90°…360° around the rim of a round plate; use it to read off the sign of sin and cos in each quadrant.

c11_math_ch04.task: Stand books or dominoes in a line and topple the first: if each falls onto the next, all fall — physical proof by mathematical induction.

c11_math_ch05.task: On graph paper draw the complex plane, plot 3+2i and −1−4i, and compute each modulus by measuring distance from the origin.

c11_math_ch06.task: You have 100 counters: item A 'costs' 30, item B 'costs' 20. List all pairs (x,y) with 30x+20y≤100 and shade the solution region on graph paper.

c11_math_ch07.task: Count real choices: how many outfits from 4 tops × 3 bottoms? Then count arrangements of 5 books on a shelf and verify it equals 5!.

c11_math_ch08.task: Write Pascal's triangle to row 6, use it to expand (x+1)⁵, and check that the coefficients sum to 2⁵.

c11_math_ch09.task: Stack coins in rows of 1,3,5,7,… and find the 10-row total using AP; then fold a paper in half repeatedly and record the doubling — AP vs GP.

c11_math_ch10.task: Use floor tiles as a grid: walk the line y=2x+1, then y=−½x; note the slopes and verify the two lines are perpendicular.

c11_math_ch11.task: Shine a phone torch on a wall while tilting it: circle → ellipse → parabola. Sketch each conic section the cone of light makes.

c11_math_ch12.task: Take your room's corner as the origin and the floor tiles as axes; estimate the (x,y,z) coordinates of 5 objects — your room in 3D.

c11_math_ch13.task: Roll a ball down a sloped tray; time it over 1 m, 50 cm and 25 cm. Compute the three average speeds and argue what the instantaneous speed must be — a limit.

c11_math_ch14.task: Write six sentences about your home; label which are statements (true/false), write the negation of each, and spot one 'and' and one 'or' compound.

c11_phy_ch01.task: Measure a room's length in foot-spans and with a tape; compare precision. Then find the thickness of one paper sheet by measuring a 100-sheet stack and dividing.

c11_phy_ch02.task: Mark distances on a sloped tray, roll a ball and time it between marks; check whether it covers equal distances in equal times — uniform vs accelerated motion.

c11_phy_ch03.task: Launch a soft ball or paper ball at ~30°, 45° and 60° indoors and measure the ranges; find which angle throws farthest — projectile motion.

c11_phy_ch04.task: Place a light cup on a smooth paper sheet and yank the paper fast — the cup stays (inertia). Then release an inflated balloon — the third law pushes it.

c11_phy_ch05.task: Time yourself climbing one flight of stairs empty-handed vs carrying a heavy bag; compute power P=mgh/t for both (estimate m and h) and compare.

c11_phy_ch06.task: Spin a raw egg and a boiled egg on a plate — which spins longer? Stop each briefly and release: the raw one restarts — internal fluid inertia.

c11_phy_ch07.task: Measure g with a pendulum: hang a key on a 1 m thread, time 20 full swings, and compute g=4π²L/T². Compare with 9.8 m/s².

c11_phy_ch08.task: Hang a rubber band and add coins one at a time to a hooked paper cup; plot extension vs load — find where it stops being proportional (elastic limit).

c11_phy_ch09.task: Float a raw egg in plain water, then stir in salt until it rises — buoyancy and density; note how much salt it took.

c11_phy_ch10.task: Put identical hot water in three cups: open, covered with a lid, wrapped in cloth. Rank their temperatures after 15 min — specific heat and insulation.

c11_phy_ch11.task: Pump a bicycle tyre fast for a minute and feel the pump barrel — compression heats the gas; then feel air escaping a balloon valve — expansion cools.

c11_phy_ch12.task: Stretch a balloon over a bottle's mouth and stand the bottle in hot water; watch it inflate — gas molecules push harder when heated.

c11_phy_ch13.task: Time 20 swings of a key-pendulum at thread lengths 25 cm, 50 cm and 100 cm; verify the period grows as √L — simple harmonic motion.

c11_phy_ch14.task: Fill identical glasses to different water levels and tap each with a spoon; order the pitches — standing waves in an air column.

c12_bio_ch01.task: Start three free clones: regrow a spring-onion stub, a carrot top and a money-plant cutting in water; log which roots first — asexual reproduction.

c12_bio_ch02.task: Gently dissect any flower onto white paper: arrange sepals, petals, stamens and pistil in order; look for pollen grains and the ovary.

c12_bio_ch03.task: Make a photo timeline of one family member from infant to adult; annotate the key developmental changes at each stage.

c12_bio_ch04.task: Draft a 6-point reproductive-health and hygiene checklist for your household (nutrition, iron-rich foods, clean habits, health awareness) and discuss it with family.

c12_bio_ch05.task: Draw a three-generation pedigree of one trait (earlobe type or tongue rolling) for your family; mark your dominant vs recessive guesses.

c12_bio_ch06.task: Extract DNA in your kitchen: mash banana with salt and a drop of dish soap, strain, then trickle ice-cold spirit/sanitiser down the side — spool the white strings.

c12_bio_ch07.task: Compare your arm bones' arrangement with a bird wing and a cat or dog leg (photos or live observation); sketch the shared plan — homology as evidence of evolution.

c12_bio_ch08.task: Do a vector audit: find any standing water (pots, coolers, tyres) around home that could breed mosquitoes; empty or cover them and log what you found.

c12_bio_ch09.task: Run a mini selection trial: sprout 10 moong seeds, keep the 3 sturdiest seedlings and discard the rest — artificial selection at home scale.

c12_bio_ch10.task: Set curd: stir a spoon of curd into warm milk and leave covered overnight; compare texture and sourness with the starter — microbes at work.

c12_bio_ch11.task: List every 'biotech' process in your kitchen — curd, dosa/idli batter rise, bread, pickles, fermentation — and name the microbe or enzyme behind each.

c12_bio_ch12.task: Hunt labels and medicine strips at home for biotech products — vaccines, insulin, fortified flour, probiotic curd; record which technology made each.

c12_bio_ch13.task: Count visitors (ants, birds, bees) to a fixed spot near a window every 15 minutes for two hours; plot the activity curve — a mini population study.

c12_chem_ch01.task: Stir salt into a fixed cup of water a spoon at a time until some stays undissolved — you've hit saturation; repeat with warm water and compare the limits.

c12_chem_ch02.task: Build a lemon battery: push a copper coin and a galvanised or iron nail into a lemon; touch the two leads briefly to your tongue — the faint tingle is electrochemistry.

c12_chem_ch03.task: Drop equal pinches of an effervescent tablet (or soda+vinegar mix) into cold and warm water; time the fizz — temperature controls reaction rate.

c12_chem_ch04.task: Round up iron/steel, copper/brass and aluminium items; test each with a magnet, note colour and tarnish — transition-metal variety at home.

c12_chem_ch05.task: Find coloured metal compounds around home: green patina on copper/brass, red-brown rust on iron, blue-green stains near old pipes — note each colour-coordination clue.

c12_chem_ch06.task: Read labels and materials at home and list organohalogen uses: PVC pipes, Teflon-coated pan, refrigerant markings, bleach or disinfectant — halogen chemistry in the house.

c12_chem_ch07.task: Put a drop of water and a drop of sanitiser/spirit on the back of each hand; compare cooling and evaporation speed — volatility of alcohols (do not ingest).

c12_chem_ch08.task: Waft-smell three kitchen items — vinegar, vanilla essence, and nail-polish remover if present — and map each odour to its functional group: acid, aldehyde, ketone/ester.

c12_chem_ch09.task: Smell fresh fish (or an egg-rich dish) before and after squeezing lemon on it; note the fishiness drop — acid neutralising volatile amines.

c12_chem_ch10.task: Run three kitchen biochem tests: grease-spot on paper (fat), heat egg white in a pan (protein denaturation), chew plain rice 30 s for sweetness (starch→sugar).

c12_math_ch01.task: Arrow-map each family member to birth month and to mother tongue; decide for each map whether it is a function, one-one, onto, or none.

c12_math_ch02.task: Tilt a plank against a step; measure rise and run, compute tan⁻¹(rise/run) for the angle, then verify with a protractor — function meets inverse.

c12_math_ch03.task: Record a month of expenses as a 3×4 matrix (3 categories × 4 weeks); add it to a second month's matrix and find the combined spend.

c12_math_ch04.task: Shift two books into a parallelogram on the table; measure its area directly, then compute it as a determinant of the two edge vectors — compare.

c12_math_ch05.task: Estimate your room's temperature each hour for a day and plot it; argue the curve is continuous and mark where it is steepest — derivative as rate of change.

c12_math_ch06.task: Cut equal squares from a sheet's corners and fold an open box; try 2–3 cut sizes, compute each volume, and find the cut that maximises it — optimisation.

c12_math_ch07.task: Estimate a room's floor area by counting full tiles then adding fractional strips — area as the limit of a sum, the idea of a definite integral.

c12_math_ch08.task: Trace a bangle's semicircle on graph paper; count squares for its area and compare with ½πr² — area under a curve.

c12_math_ch09.task: Record a hot cup's temperature every 5 minutes as it cools; show the cooling rate shrinks as the cup nears room temperature — dT/dt = −k(T−Troom).

c12_math_ch10.task: From your room's centre walk '3 tiles east, 4 north'; measure the straight-line displacement — vector addition and magnitude 5.

c12_math_ch11.task: Hold two pencils so they are neither parallel nor intersecting — skew lines in your room's 3D space; use a taut string to visualise the shortest distance between them.

c12_math_ch12.task: Maximise protein: pick two foods with known protein and price, set a fixed budget constraint, plot the feasible region and find the corner-point optimum.

c12_math_ch13.task: From a shuffled deck draw two cards without replacement, 20 trials; estimate P(both red) and compare with (26/52)×(25/51).

c12_phy_ch01.task: Rub a balloon on dry hair or wool; pick up paper bits, then bend a thin stream of tap water with it — charge by friction and induction.

c12_phy_ch02.task: Stick a charged balloon to a wall and time how long it holds; try a humid vs dry day — charge leaks, and stored charge links to capacitance.

c12_phy_ch03.task: Compare charging: note battery % gained in 15 minutes on two different cables or adapters; relate the difference to current and cable resistance (observe only, no dismantling).

c12_phy_ch04.task: Lay a compass beside an appliance cord while it runs vs switched off; look for needle deflection — Oersted's discovery in your wiring.

c12_phy_ch05.task: Magnetise a steel needle by stroking it 30 times one way on a fridge magnet; test it on a pin, then drop it repeatedly and retest — magnetism made and lost.

c12_phy_ch06.task: On an induction cooktop (if you have one) briefly test empty steel vs aluminium vs ceramic bowls — only magnetic cookware responds; explain eddy-current heating.

c12_phy_ch07.task: Note '50 Hz' on an appliance label; wave a phone torch fast in a dark room to see persistence of vision — why AC flicker is invisible to us.

c12_phy_ch08.task: Map the EM spectrum in your house: FM radio, microwave oven, TV-remote IR, sunlight's UV warming, Wi-Fi — list a device per band.

c12_phy_ch09.task: Stand a pencil in a glass of water — it appears bent; then drop a coin in a mug and note how much shallower it looks — refraction and apparent depth.

c12_phy_ch10.task: Tilt a CD or DVD under a lamp to spread rainbow streaks — a diffraction grating; then view a bulb through stretched thin cloth for a diffraction pattern.

c12_phy_ch11.task: If your home has a solar calculator or garden light, cover half its cell and watch the display or light fade — light itself ejects charge: the photoelectric effect.

c12_phy_ch12.task: Compare a candle's yellow flame with the blue of an LPG stove from a safe distance; relate the colours to how much energy each atom or molecule releases.

c12_phy_ch13.task: Build scale intuition: if an atom were your entire house, its nucleus is a grain of rice at the centre; compute that size ratio (atom ~10⁻¹⁰ m, nucleus ~10⁻¹⁵ m).

c12_phy_ch14.task: List 5 semiconductor devices at home — LED bulb, charger rectifier, remote control, phone chip, solar cell — and name what each does with electrons.

c6_biology_ch06.task: Start a height chart on a wall: mark and date your height, then re-measure monthly; also log one change in sleep or appetite — tracking adolescence.

c6_biology_ch09.task: Count your breaths per minute at rest, then after 30 jumping jacks; record both and explain why your body demanded more air.

c6_biology_ch10.task: Stand a celery stalk or white flower in a glass of water coloured with turmeric or food colour; check after a few hours where the colour climbed — water transport.

c6_chemistry_ch04.task: Sort 10 household items into a property table: transparent/opaque, hard/soft, floats/sinks, magnetic or not — materials chosen by properties.

c6_chemistry_ch05.task: List six changes you can watch at home — melting ice, boiling water, curd setting, a nail rusting, dough rising, paper tearing — and classify each reversible or irreversible.

c6_physics_ch01.task: Do a science scavenger hunt: find one push, one pull, one thing melting, one thing evaporating and one living response in your home today.

c6_physics_ch02.task: Sit by a window for 15 minutes and write five 'why' questions from what you see (ants, shadows, birds, leaves); pick one and test it at home.

c6_physics_ch03.task: Build a simple tester — a battery, a torch bulb or LED from an old toy, and wires — and test which items conduct: coin, key, rubber, pencil lead, plastic.

c6_physics_ch07.task: Wrap identical cups of hot water in cotton cloth, newspaper and nothing; check which stays warmest after 15 minutes — insulators slow heat loss.

c6_physics_ch08.task: Mark a 20 m path in your corridor or veranda; time yourself walking, fast-walking and running it; compute the three speeds.

c6_physics_ch11.task: Trace your shadow's outline at 9 am, noon and 4 pm on the same spot; compare lengths and directions — the sun's apparent movement.

c6_physics_ch12.task: In a dark room, model an eclipse: a torch for the sun, a big ball for earth and a small ball for the moon — arrange them to recreate solar and lunar eclipses.

c7_bio_ch01.task: Keep a 3-day log of sleep hours, water intake and activity; rate your energy each evening and spot what growing bodies need most.

c7_bio_ch02.task: Wrap a tape around your chest, then take the deepest breath you can and record the expansion — your lungs' living bellows.

c7_bio_ch03.task: Tie a clear plastic bag around a leafy twig overnight; check for droplets inside in the morning — transpiration caught in the act.

c7_chem_ch01.task: Take a fridge magnet on a tour: test 12 household items and tabulate magnetic vs non-magnetic — then separate the magnetic metals from the rest.

c7_chem_ch02.task: Dissolve salt in water, then evaporate it on a plate in the sun to recover the salt — a reversible change; try the same with lime or chalk paste and compare.

c7_physics_ch01.task: Write five testable questions about your own home (which mug keeps tea hottest? which room is coolest?) — pick one and run a fair test.

c7_physics_ch02.task: Wire two torch bulbs on batteries: first one-after-another (series), then side-by-side (parallel); remove one bulb each time — which keeps the other lit?

c7_physics_ch03.task: Leave a steel spoon and a wooden spoon in a hot pan with handles out; touch-test which handle heats first — conduction; then hold your palm above vs beside a warm vessel — convection vs radiation.

c7_physics_ch04.task: Make a water clock: pierce a small hole near a bottle's base, let it drip into a marked cup, and calibrate 'one minute' against a real clock.

c7_physics_ch05.task: Build a pinhole viewer: a card with a pinhole plus a tracing-paper screen in a darkened room; watch the bright window scene appear upside-down.

c7_physics_ch06.task: With a torch (sun) and a ball (earth), show day and night by rotating the ball; then orbit a small ball (moon) and note its changing lit face — phases.

c7_physics_ch07.task: Rub soap solution on turmeric-smeared paper — it turns red; dab lemon juice to reverse it — your own acid-base indicator from the kitchen.

c8_bio_ch01.task: Seal a moist bread slice in a container and check daily with a magnifier for mould colonies — the invisible world made visible (don't touch or sniff; discard sealed).

c8_bio_ch02.task: Track sleep, water and exercise for 7 days and rate your daily energy; find which habit most predicts how you feel.

c8_chem_ch02.task: Drop equal sugar into a cup of hot and of cold water without stirring; time which dissolves first — particles move faster when warm.

c8_chem_ch03.task: Separate a home-made mixture (salt+sand or rice+small stones) using sieving, dissolving and evaporating; record which technique removed which component.

c8_physics_ch01.task: Run a fair test on paper planes: keep the paper the same, change only wing design or nose weight across 3 throws each — which variable changes range most?

c8_physics_ch02.task: Wrap 20 turns of insulated wire around an iron nail, touch the ends to a battery briefly, and count pins it lifts — an electromagnet (disconnect so it doesn't heat).

c8_physics_ch03.task: Push a notebook, then a full bucket, across floor vs carpet; rank the force needed — friction and load in your living room.

c8_physics_ch04.task: Fill a glass brim-full, cover with a card, and invert over a sink — the card stays: air pressure at work; then slowly tilt it.

c8_physics_ch05.task: Make three mixtures — salt+water, sugar+water, oil+water; name solute and solvent in each, then leave drops on plates and see which leave a residue.

c8_physics_ch06.task: Compare your face in a steel spoon's two sides (concave vs convex), then place a water drop on clear plastic over text — a droplet magnifier.

c8_physics_ch07.task: Sketch the moon's shape from your window each clear night for a week at the same time; label the waxing or waning phase.

c8_physics_ch08.task: Watch a crumb trail: crumbs→ants→spider or gecko near your home; draw the food chain you actually observed.

c8_physics_ch09.task: Measure midday temperature in three spots — direct sun, shade, indoors; compare and link to why Earth sustains life (atmosphere, water, distance from sun).

c9_bio_ch01.task: Peel onion membrane onto a glass slide or damp glass, add a drop of water, and view through a magnifier or phone macro; sketch the cell boundaries you see.

c9_bio_ch02.task: Snap a celery stalk and pull — notice the 'strings' (vascular tissue) resist; compare with how a soft leaf tears — tissues differ by job.

c9_bio_ch03.task: Regrow from scraps: stand a carrot top or sweet potato in water and log where roots vs shoots emerge — one organism, many reproductive modes.

c9_bio_ch04.task: Build a mini field guide: photograph or sketch 8 organisms around your home (insects, plants, birds, moulds) and group them by visible features.

c9_chem_ch01.task: Evaporate equal drops of salt water and sugar water on two plates; compare the residues — solutions are mixtures hiding pure substances.

c9_chem_ch02.task: Weigh equal volumes of water, oil and rice in the same cup on a kitchen scale; rank their masses — same space, different packing of particles.

c9_chem_ch03.task: Use your battery-and-bulb tester: dip the two leads in salt water, sugar water and plain water — which conducts? Ionic vs covalent in a cup.

c9_physics_ch01.task: Measure your study table three ways — handspans, notebook-widths, ruler; compare the answers and explain why standard units exist.

c9_physics_ch02.task: Time yourself covering a fixed 30 m at slow, normal and fast pace; compute the three speeds and draw a bar graph of you.

c9_physics_ch03.task: Stack 5 coins and flick the bottom one out — the stack drops straight down; then try the card-and-coin trick over a glass — inertia demos.

c9_physics_ch04.task: Lift a filled 5 L bottle vs an empty one to shoulder height 10 times; note the effort difference — work = force × distance.

c9_physics_ch05.task: Make a string telephone: two paper cups joined by a taut string; talk through it, then slacken the string and compare — sound needs a medium.

c9_physics_ch06.task: Plant a straight stick in a sunny spot; mark its shadow tip each hour — find local noon (shortest shadow) and trace the sun's path.
